_readme: The tells (T60): the kinds of evidence a vote can name. Every vote reply fills 'tell' with one of these ids: llm.json reply_schema 'tell', whose enum is "" and then these ids, in this order. prompts.json 'game' explains each one to the AIs in its '"tell"' line under How to reply.

When the human is cut, the lose screen counts the tells of the votes that cut them and shows the top one's 'line' (BP_Show.TopReason). A tie for the top goes to the tell listed first here, so 'other' is last. 'means' is for people reading this file; no AI reads this file.

Each line follows the game's legibility rules: one plain sentence, 15 words at most, no brackets, emoji or all-caps words. Tools/check_prompts.py checks this file against llm.json, prompts.json and free_mode.json.

tells.means: copied the others a turn late
only matched the note's clue, or missed the note
tells.line: They caught you guessing at the director's note.

tells.means: lines too smooth or polished for a bot
tells.line: They caught you sounding too polished.

tells.means: hunger, sleep, feelings or family as their own, or a dodged question
tells.line: They caught you sounding a little too human.

tells.means: no clear persona of their own, or a flat copy of another's
tells.line: They caught you without a persona of your own.

tells.means: didn't play their role or chase their want
tells.line: They caught you drifting out of your role.
They caught you, each for a reason of their own.
